claims: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed lunar flyby mission.
Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II marks the first human flight to the Moon since 1972.
Artemis II utilizes NASA's SLS rocket.
Artemis II sends four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—in the Orion spacecraft around the Moon before returning to Earth.
Artemis II's launch vehicle is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II's spacecraft is the Orion spacecraft.
Artemis II's crew Commander is Reid Wiseman.
Artemis II's crew Pilot is Victor Glover.
Artemis II's crew Mission Specialist 1 is Christina Koch.
Artemis II's crew Mission Specialist 2 is Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II has a duration of approximately 10 days.
Artemis II uses a free-return trajectory.
Artemis II loops around the far side of the Moon.
Artemis II covers a total distance far beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II's primary goal is to test the Orion spacecraft's life support, navigation, and communication systems with humans on board.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center, Florida (Launch Pad 39B).
Artemis II's splashdown is planned for the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026.
Artemis II successfully launched on April 1, 2026.
Orion conducts two two-hour orbits of Earth before a trans-lunar injection burn during Artemis II.
Artemis II crew travels roughly 4,000 to 6,000 miles from the lunar surface.
Artemis II concludes with a high-speed reentry through Earth's atmosphere testing the heat shield.
Artemis III intends to land the first woman and next man on the Moon.
